title: Affine derived base-change comparison map and its localization
statement: Let R\to A and R\to R' be ring maps and put A'=A\otimes_R R'. For a complex M^\bullet of A-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] there is a canonical comparison morphism [def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology] c:M^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'\to M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A' in D(R') (Stacks, More on Algebra, equation comparison-map): it is E^\bullet\otimes_R R'\to P^\bullet\otimes_A A' for a K-flat complex P^\bullet of A-modules representing M^\bullet and a quasi-isomorphism E^\bullet\to P^\bullet from a K-flat complex E^\bullet of R-modules [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For every i, H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A') has its evident A'-module structure, while H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R') is an A'-module as follows: a in A acts by H^i(a\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{id}_{R'}) through End_{D(A)}(M^\bullet)\to End_{D(R)}(M^\bullet)\to End_{D(R')}(M^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'), and this action commutes with R', hence combines to an A'=A\otimes_R R' action. With these structures H^i(c) is A'-linear. For every prime \mathfrak q' of A', with images \mathfrak q of A and \mathfrak p',\mathfrak p of R',R, there are natural isomorphisms H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R')\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'}\cong H^i(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}R'_{\mathfrak p'})\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}R'_{\mathfrak p'}}A'_{\mathfrak q'} and H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A')\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'}\cong H^i(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_{\mathfrak q}}A'_{\mathfrak q'}), under which H^i(c)\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'} is the map induced by the comparison morphism for R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}, R_{\mathfrak p}\to R'_{\mathfrak p'} followed by scalar extension along A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}R'_{\mathfrak p'}\to A'_{\mathfrak q'}.

proof.text: For exists_affineDerivedBaseChangeComparison, use spanLeft_isIso from def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology in every degree. The left span arrow is therefore a quasi-isomorphism; DerivedCategory.isIso_Q_map_iff_quasiIso and pointwise invertibility make its Q-whiskering invertible. Define c as its inverse followed by the Q-whiskering of spanRight. Cancellation proves the span equation and uniqueness; naturality of DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors and cancellation prove the cohomology equation.

proof.text: For the arbitrary-model clause, the existing functorial flatResolution of ModuleCat supplies K-flat values and quasi-isomorphic augmentations via LeftResolution.kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj and quasiIso_resolutionNatTrans_app. Naturality of the augmentation and two-of-three show that resolution preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Apply the existing CochainComplex.scalarExtension_quasiIso_of_kFlat from lem-sc-kflat-scalar-extension-derived-iso (accessed by proof-only import all) to preserve quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes under ordinary scalar extension. For an A-K-flat quasi-isomorphism apply the same fact over A with coefficient A tensor_R B, then restrict to B. The generator formulas of lem-pc-base-tensor-ordinary-iso give a commuting Arrow.isoMk that transports this result to extend R B after restrict R A.

For given quasi-isomorphisms p:P→M and e:E→restrict(P), set es to the inverse of Q(extend(augmentation E)) followed by Q(extend(resolution(e≫restrict(p)))). Set et to the inverse of Q(extend(restrict(augmentation P))) followed by Q(targetComplex(p)). Every map inverted is an isomorphism by the preceding step. These formulas give both augmentation equations. Cancel the left span arrow and apply augmentation naturality to obtain c(P)≫Q(extend(restrict(augmentation P))) = Q(extend(augmentation(restrict P))). Augmentation naturality at e and c-naturality at p then prove es.hom≫c(M)=Q(extend(e))≫et.hom. This proves the entire first Lean declaration without new holes.

proof.text: Remaining plan for exists_affineDerivedBaseChangeLocalization (not proved in this delivery): The target complex P^\bullet\otimes_A A' is a complex of A'-modules. On the source cohomology, define the A-action by applying H^i to the endomorphism a\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{id}_{R'} induced by a in End_{D(A)}(M^\bullet), then compose restriction of scalars to D(R) and derived tensor with R'. The resulting A-action commutes with the scalar R'-action, so it extends to A'. Naturality of c in M^\bullet (Step 1), applied to the endomorphisms a of M^\bullet, makes H^i(c) A'-linear.

source.place: Tag 0DJ8, affine proof, A'-linearity of the comparison map

proof.text: Remaining plan for exists_affineDerivedBaseChangeLocalization (not proved in this delivery): For a prime \mathfrak q' of A' with images \mathfrak q, \mathfrak p' and \mathfrak p, the source isomorphism H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R')\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'}\cong H^i(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}R'_{\mathfrak p'})\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}R'_{\mathfrak p'}}A'_{\mathfrak q'}, for the A'-action of Step 4, and its compatibility with c are [lem-pc-derived-tensor-localization-cohomology]; no A'-localization of the R-complex E^\bullet\otimes_R R' is used. For the target, only the A-complex P^\bullet is localized: P^\bullet_{\mathfrak q} is K-flat over A_{\mathfrak q} (for an acyclic A_{\mathfrak q}-complex F^\bullet, F^\bullet\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}}P^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}=F^\bullet\otimes_A P^\bullet) and represents M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}, and the localization-of-tensor-products identification [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] gives (P^\bullet\otimes_A A')\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'}\cong P^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}}A'_{\mathfrak q'}, a model of M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_{\mathfrak q}}A'_{\mathfrak q'}.

source.place: Tag 0DJ8, affine proof, displayed localization identities

proof.text: Remaining plan for exists_affineDerivedBaseChangeLocalization (not proved in this delivery): For the A'-complexes P^\bullet\otimes_A A' and their localizations, localization is exact [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so kernels and images of differentials localize and H^i(C)\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'}\cong H^i(C\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'}). Applying this to the target complex and using Step 5 gives the two stated cohomology isomorphisms. Naturality of the tensor maps gives that H^i(c)\otimes_{A'}A'_{\mathfrak q'} is induced by the localized comparison followed by the stated scalar extension.
